_comment: Fundraising proposal for Moonshot Foundry (Jeff Brown). Built from three discovery calls: Aug 26 strategy call, Sep 21 pricing/process call with Freizle. One LinkedIn profile (Jeff's), scaling to more accounts later. Includes the Foundry-pipeline partnership context Jeff asked to have woven in.

cards.label: THE ASK
cards.text: $3–5M growth raise for Moonshot Foundry, floor $3M, ideally committed by year-end. Funds go-to-market scaling and infrastructure, about 25% into tech platform expansion, and about 20% into the Foundry operations behind 10–12 new InsurTech launches a year.

cards.label: THE PLAN
cards.text: Your LinkedIn profile, run end to end by ThinkFISH in your voice. Targeting investors who already think in InsurTech terms, family offices, angels and the wave of new InsurTech-focused funds, instead of generalist VCs who need convincing from zero. Every meeting pre-qualified and approved by you.

cards.label: THE INVESTMENT
cards.text: $2,500 per month for one account, or $3,000 for two, flat. Six-month term with a three-month opt-out. No setup fee, no success fee, no commission, no transaction involvement.

band.label: WHAT TO EXPECT
band.text: Outreach live within two weeks of kickoff. First qualified investor conversations in weeks three and four, building to a steady 1–3 qualified meetings per week from month two, with weekly reporting and a data-driven checkpoint at the three-month opt-out. One honest note: early-growth raises historically take 6–12 months from first outreach to capital in the bank, in line with what you've already budgeted for. We can have the right investors on your calendar quickly; whether commitments close by year-end depends on your process and each investor's diligence, and we'd rather you hear that from us now.

gap.narrative: You've built something real: three rolled-up InsurTech businesses running about $2M this year, a Foundry model already producing two live joint ventures, and roughly $1.1M raised through your own network. What's stalling isn't the story, it's the audience. VCs keep passing because the aggregation-plus-incubation model doesn't fit a pure SaaS or pure-AI thesis, and your own network, tapped for everything it has, is now returning 5–10% response rates on cold outreach.
gap.principle: Your raise isn't short on interest, it's short on investors who already speak InsurTech and don't need weeks of education before a check gets written. Finding that specific pool at volume is a targeting problem, not a pitch problem.
rows: Warm network capped near $1.1M committed; cold outreach off your own AI-built list is landing 5–10% response, well below the volume a $3–5M raise needs.
Go-to-market scaling, the 25% tech platform build-out and the 20% Foundry allocation behind 10–12 planned launches a year, all wait on capital that hasn't closed.
You're running three companies and a launch pipeline while also sourcing investors and educating generalists on a niche most outsiders don't understand.
Every month spent explaining the model to the wrong investor pushes the close further past year-end and delays the next round of Foundry launches behind it.

segments.name: InsurTech-Native Angels & Family Offices
segments.why: A documented InsurTech thesis and similar checks written in the last 12 months, the investors who need no education on the market.

segments.name: New InsurTech-Focused Funds
segments.why: First-time managers launching funds built specifically around InsurTech, 100+ opened in the last 18 months, actively deploying.

segments.name: Complementary-Vertical Operators
segments.why: Angels and family offices experienced in SaaS, fintech or payments who've shown willingness to stretch into adjacent verticals.

segments.name: Roll-Up & Portfolio-Model Investors
segments.why: Investors comfortable backing an aggregation-plus-incubation structure rather than a single-product SaaS story.

icp.note: This is our starting point. The full target outline, including check sizes and exclusions, gets planned with you during onboarding.

architecture.title: This Raise, and the Partnership Beyond
architecture.subtitle: HOW ONE ENGAGEMENT SUPPORTS THE FOUNDRY MODEL

cards.label: THE MOONSHOT RAISE
cards.text: This engagement runs the $3–5M growth raise for Moonshot Foundry itself, the capital behind go-to-market scaling, the tech platform build-out and the Foundry operations that power 10–12 new InsurTech launches a year.

cards.label: THE FOUNDRY PIPELINE
cards.text: Each MGA, JV or InsurTech launch that follows carries its own future raise and its own future investor conversations, the same problem you're solving today, repeated roughly a dozen times a year.

cards.label: A STANDING PARTNERSHIP
cards.text: Once the model is proven on this raise, the same account team and targeting are ready for each subsequent venture's capital raise, without rebuilding trust or process from zero every time.

band.label: WHY THIS MATTERS NOW
band.text: You asked us to weave in how a longer-term relationship across future launches could work. Proving the model on Moonshot's own raise is the fastest way there: once we know how to find InsurTech-literate capital for you, the same engine can point at each new venture, cyber MGAs, AI-agent insurance, whatever launches next, without starting from zero.

cards.label: OUTREACH VOLUME
cards.text: 800 InMails and 800 connection invites every month from your profile, once fully warmed up. Every touch scored and hand-reviewed before it goes out.

cards.label: QUALIFIED MEETINGS
cards.unit: per week at steady state (month 2 onward)
cards.text: Conservatively 1–3 per week from one account once calibrated. Add a second account and the range moves with it.

cards.label: TIME TO FIRST MEETINGS
cards.unit: weeks from kickoff to first booked calls
cards.text: Weeks one and two are setup: ICP, audiences, scripts, profile warm-up. Live outreach starts in week three, first replies and bookings follow within days.

columns.label: MONTH 3  ·  DECEMBER
columns.title: Prove-Out & Scale
bullets: Scale: add accounts, or next raise

band.label: THE DECEMBER CHECKPOINT
band.text: By the December review you'll have three months of real numbers on audience quality, meeting quality and conversions. That's your three-month opt-out checkpoint: continue, add a second account, or stop. When the Foundry's next venture is ready to raise, the same account team and engine are already calibrated to InsurTech capital.

cards.label: 1  ·  REVIEW
cards.text: Take this to your co-founders and send us the questions that come back. If it helps, Freizle will join a 20-minute call with your team to field the technical, targeting and compliance questions directly.

cards.label: 2  ·  SIGN & KICK OFF
cards.text: We send the services agreement the same day you say yes. Onboarding starts that week: one 60-minute interview, and we connect your LinkedIn profile to our system, no passwords required.

cards.label: 3  ·  FIRST MEETINGS
cards.text: Your profile is live within two weeks of kickoff. The first qualified investor conversations land on your calendar in weeks three and four, then build to a steady weekly rhythm through your December checkpoint.

band.label: WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
band.text: Connect your LinkedIn account to our system (no passwords or login credentials required). Share your target list, past investor conversations and anyone who's already passed. One 60-minute onboarding interview. A Calendly link, and a do-not-contact list if there's anyone we should avoid. That's it. We handle the rest.
